svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.23.9.2 Joists Supported by Beams
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.9.2 Joists Supported by Beams
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Joists Supported by Beams

g.text: Joists on the top of the beam, (1)
Framed into the side of a wood beam:
Ledger strip nailed to the side of the beam,
also has four 89 mm nails to the beam, (2)(b)
600 mm or longer above the beam, (4)
On 38 × 38 bolted to the web, bolts 6.3 mm
diam or more, 600 mm or less apart, (3)
Steel beam, lumber on the web

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Floor joists may be supported on the tops of beams
or may be framed into the sides of beams.
When framed into the side of a wood beam, joists are
supported on
(a) joist hangers or other acceptable mechanical
connectors, or (b) not less than 38 mm by 64 mm ledger
strips nailed to the side of the beam, except that 38 mm
by 38 mm ledger strips may be used provided each joist
is nailed to the beam by not less than four 89 mm nails,
in addition to the nailing for the ledger strip required
in Table 9.23.3.4.
When framed into the side of a steel beam, joists
are supported on the bottom flange of the beam or on
not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber bolted to the
web with not less than 6.3 mm diam bolts spaced not
more than 600 mm apart.
Joists referred to in Sentence (3) are spliced above
the beam with not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber at
least 600 mm long to support the flooring.
Not less than a 12 mm space is provided between the
splice and the beam to allow for shrinkage of the
wood joists.
Drawn: generic hangers, no make or model. Ledger nailing from Table 9.23.3.4. Nail and bolt positions are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.9.2. (page 9-179)
